data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 argues that centralization is more resilient because it enables coordinated, rapid responses. But it fails the problem's core distinction by ignoring correlated failure entirely in its resilience claim. Its own counterconditions concede the central control plane is an SPOF for a correlated crash and that homogeneity makes all redundant nodes vulnerable to the same 'poison pill'. These are not marginal edge-cases: they are the precise class of correlated failure the problem asks about. The target's mechanism (fast kill-switch, active-active load balancing) cannot help when the shared control plane or shared software bug is itself the trigger, so the argument asserts greater resilience while conceding the correlated-failure pathway that defeats it.
